findings.location: ## Statement, displayed estimate with C e^{Ct}; SI interpretation in Remarks
findings.evidence: The fixed-gauge definition and theorem Remarks set t=x^0 in metres and the normalized state norm to be dimensionless. In the homogeneous estimate, the leading C multiplying the norm ratio must be dimensionless, while the C in e^{Ct} must have units m^{-1}. One constant cannot serve both roles. The proof supports the abstract real-coordinate estimate, but its stated SI interpretation needs separate dimensioned constants or dimensionless time, with a matching forcing normalization.

findings.location: ## Statement, paragraph beginning “Fix a compact parameter interval”
findings.evidence: The claim requires K to be a compact subset of the “position-velocity phase space” but does not define that space before using it. The proof later uses coordinates (x,v), but the Statement should specify the object, e.g. TU={(p,v):p∈U, v∈T_pM} in the common chart, so compactness and the geodesic lifts have an exact domain.

findings.location: ## Statement, sentence stating both proper times are ℓ/c
findings.evidence: The Statement assigns x^0 and the interval length ℓ metres but does not state the unit of c or the resulting proper-time unit. The mathematical supplier def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time treats c as a positive real and its Remarks defer physical dimensions to def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions, which sets c in m s^{-1} and proper time in seconds. State this SI reading locally so ℓ/c is dimensioned as a duration.
